This can be interpreted in two ways.

First interpretation: Zoe Quinn wants to establish that people have to believe her/other accusers of wrongdoing if allegations are made. She wants to enforce punishment through international legislation and monitoring anonymous people.

Second interpretation: Zoe Quinn wants to shift the burden of proof upon the accused. If someone can’t prove he is innocent he should be punished according to upcoming international legislation.

And this should be done without questioning the allegations of the accuser and shifting the burden of proof on the accused. She wants people of certain demographics to work in tech to address the issues, though the users should be anonymous. She wants every tech company to side with her and take part in this, so there are many varieties to punish an individual being accused of wrongdoing. She wants herself and her peer-groups to be judge and executioner in one person after „proper“ legislation is adopted.

The general legal burden of proof can be described by this: „The necessity of proof always lies with the person who lays charges“ or simpler „the one who wants something has to prove that the legal requirements are met“. And since she is talking in context of violence, criminal acts or „should be criminal acts“, legally speaking we are getting in the realms of criminal justice. If not criminal justice in a sense of punishment by the government - though I can see this as a possible next step - then at least a punishment by privately owned companies because of unproven allegations of an accuser and biased people of certain demographics sitting in every tech company.

If you ask legal professionals about the principle of the "presumption of innocence“ in criminal trials, every single one of them and I mean everyone, really every legal professional will tell you, that this is one of the fundamental principles our criminal justice system is based upon.

If my word isn’t enough:

The United Nations General Assembly has adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights on 10 Dezember 1948. Article 11, Section 1 of the U.N. Universal Declaration of Human Rights states:

Article 11. (1) Everyone charged with a penal offence has the right to be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law in a public trial at which he has had all the guarantees necessary for his defence.

This is the human right of "presumption of innocence“ in criminal justice adopted by the United Nations in 1948.
